title: 2026 elections: Early voting to expand across Chicago, suburban Cook County as officials unveil new ballot-tracking technology - ABC7 Chicago

 Early voting to expand across Chicago, suburban Cook County as officials unveil new ballot tracking 
 Expanded early voting will begin Monday across Chicago and suburban Cook County. Election officials have unveiled new ballot-tracking technology. By Michelle Gallardo Monday, October 19, 2026 3:49AM Share COOK COUNTY, Ill. (WLS) -- Expanded early voting begins Monday at dozens of locations across suburban Cook County and all 50 Chicago wards. Cook County officials have unveiled new technology aimed at making the voting process more efficient and transparent.
 More than 10% of registered voters in suburban Cook County are expected to vote by mail this year. While email ballot tracking is not new, officials said new technology will provide voters with more detailed information about their ballots.
 ABC7 Chicago is now streaming 24/7. Click here to watch 
 Expanded early voting will be available at 56 locations throughout suburban Cook County beginning Monday. Voters will find smart ballot drop boxes that, combined with new technology, will allow them to track their ballots from beginning to end, including detailed U.S. Postal Service data.
 "There's over 200,000 mail ballots sent out and we track six categories of that," said Dheeraj Patri, chief technology officer at KNOWiNK.
 Cook County Deputy Clerk for Elections Ed Michalowski said the system will give voters more information about where their ballots are during the process.
 "What's good for the public is they have confidence where that mail ballot is going. all the way down to our carrier route and back to our office," Michalowski said.
 RELATED | 2026 midterm elections: Voter information in Illinois, Indiana, Wisconsin 
 Improved mail ballot tracking is one of several enhancements being made in Cook County this year. Officials also unveiled new software designed to help them see when voters check in, monitor activity at polling places and flag locations that may need attention.
 Officials hope the technology will also help them combat misinformation being spread online.
 "There will be misinformation and disinformation, but we are tackling it one step at a time," Cook County Clerk Monica Gordon said.
 SEE ALSO | Our Chicago: Race for U.S. Senate in Illinois 
 Early voting began in Chicago on Oct. 1 and in suburban Cook County on Oct. 7 but has so far been limited to a couple of downtown sites and a handful of locations across the suburbs.
 While turnout is generally lower in midterm election years than in presidential election years, voter interest this year is higher than usual.
 "Chicago, for better or for worse has been on the national stage and I think it has raised people's desire to have an impact, regardless of what side of the aisle you're on," Chicago voter Rob Brown said.
 SEE ALSO | Our Chicago: Candidates for CPS board president make their case to voters 
 In addition to the suburban Cook County expansion, early voting will expand to all 50 Chicago wards beginning Monday, with polling places opening at 9 a.m.
